cues.text: A Kodiak woman asked Google when
snipe season opens.
She told troopers its AI
answer said September first.
So on September fifth she shot three snipe.
At home she opened the state
regulations and saw her mistake.
She called troopers and turned herself in.
The trooper's report says the general
season opened October eighth.
So the answer and the report disagreed.
That trooper ran her exact search.
He got the same wrong answer.
So which page can a hunter trust?
She pleaded no contest and paid
a hundred fifty dollars.
She told the Alaska Beacon, I feel terrible.
State spokesman Austin McDaniel
says he thinks it's the first
time AI has been cited.
He expects more.
Weren't there warnings?
There were.
Google's help page says AI answers may include mistakes,
and to check more than one place.
Google didn't respond to the Beacon's
request for comment on the wrong answer.
McDaniel says the one source of truth is Fish and Game's regulations
and emergency orders.
But that source has a catch.
Fish and Game's own page says
its online regulations are simplified,
and emergency orders can override them.
So even the official page is a simplified summary of state law.
The answer was on top. What counts sits underneath, the regulations
and any emergency order.
Check them first. Fish and Game will mail you the regulations,
or you can call the office.
Before you hunt, what do you check?
